list_managed_clusters.title: List AKS clusters in the subscription
list_managed_clusters.description: List every AKS cluster in the subscription, across all resource groups, with each one's Kubernetes version, node pools, FQDN, network profile and provisioning state. The place to start when the cluster's resource group is not already known.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: Every AKS cluster in the subscription.

items.description: id, name, location, sku and properties (kubernetesVersion, agentPoolProfiles, fqdn, provisioningState, powerState).

list_managed_clusters_by_resource_group.title: List AKS clusters in a resource group
list_managed_clusters_by_resource_group.description: List the AKS clusters in one resource group with their versions, node pools and provisioning state. Cheaper than scanning the whole subscription when the group is known.

resource_group.description: Name of the resource group.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The AKS clusters in the resource group.

get_managed_cluster.title: Get an AKS cluster
get_managed_cluster.description: Read one cluster's full ARM resource -- Kubernetes version, every node pool with its VM size and count, the API server FQDN, network and identity profiles, enabled add-ons, and provisioningState. Poll this after any mutating call to watch provisioningState return to "Succeeded".

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The cluster resource.

properties.description: kubernetesVersion, currentKubernetesVersion, dnsPrefix, fqdn, agentPoolProfiles, networkProfile, addonProfiles, provisioningState, powerState.

create_or_update_managed_cluster.title: Create or replace an AKS cluster
create_or_update_managed_cluster.description: Create a cluster, or replace an existing one's definition -- which is also how a cluster is upgraded, by sending a higher kubernetes_version. This is a full PUT: read the cluster with get_managed_cluster, amend the object, and send it back, or properties you omit are reset. Asynchronous; an upgrade of a production cluster takes many minutes per node pool.

resource_group.description: Resource group to create the cluster in.

location.description: Azure region for the cluster, e.g. westeurope.

kubernetes_version.description: Kubernetes version to run. Raising it on an existing cluster is how an upgrade is triggered; list_kubernetes_versions says what is available.

dns_prefix.description: DNS prefix for the API server FQDN. Required on create, immutable after.

agent_pool_profiles.description: Node pools, each with name, count, vmSize, mode (System or User), osType and osDiskSizeGB. At least one System pool is required.

network_profile.description: Network plugin, policy, service and pod CIDRs, and load balancer SKU.

api_server_access_profile.description: API server exposure, e.g. {"enablePrivateCluster": true} or authorizedIPRanges.

addon_profiles.description: Add-ons to enable, e.g. omsagent for Container Insights or azurepolicy.

auto_scaler_profile.description: Cluster autoscaler tuning -- scan interval, scale-down delays, thresholds.

aad_profile.description: Microsoft Entra ID integration and Azure RBAC for Kubernetes authorisation.

enable_rbac.description: Whether Kubernetes RBAC is enabled. Immutable after creation.

node_resource_group.description: Name for the managed resource group holding the cluster's nodes and disks.

sku.description: Cluster tier, e.g. {"name": "Base", "tier": "Standard"} for the SLA-backed tier.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The cluster resource as accepted, with provisioning in progress.

update_managed_cluster_tags.title: Update an AKS cluster's tags
update_managed_cluster_tags.description: Merge new tags into a cluster without touching anything else. This is the only field the PATCH form of the API accepts -- version, node pools and profiles all go through create_or_update_managed_cluster.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

tags.description: Tags to set on the cluster, as key/value pairs.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The cluster resource after the tag update.

delete_managed_cluster.title: Delete an AKS cluster
delete_managed_cluster.description: Delete a cluster and the managed node resource group behind it -- every node, disk and load balancer it created. Workloads and any data on ephemeral storage go with it. Not recoverable; confirm the cluster name with get_managed_cluster first.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

cluster_name.description: Name of the cluster to delete.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty; deletion runs asynchronously and reports through the azure-asyncoperation header.

start_cluster.title: Start a stopped AKS cluster
start_cluster.description: Bring a stopped cluster back up -- the control plane and every node pool. Nodes take several minutes to become Ready, and pods reschedule from scratch. Only valid on a cluster whose powerState is Stopped.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

cluster_name.description: Name of the cluster to start.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty; the operation runs asynchronously, tracked by the azure-asyncoperation header.

stop_cluster.title: Stop an AKS cluster
stop_cluster.description: Shut the cluster's control plane and nodes down so it stops charging for compute. Every running pod is terminated; persistent volumes survive. Cluster state is kept for up to twelve months, after which the cluster cannot be started again.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

cluster_name.description: Name of the cluster to stop.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty; the operation runs asynchronously, tracked by the azure-asyncoperation header.

list_cluster_admin_credentials.title: Get a cluster's admin kubeconfig
list_cluster_admin_credentials.description: Return the cluster-admin kubeconfig, which grants unrestricted access to the Kubernetes API and bypasses Entra ID entirely. The value is base64 and must be decoded before use. Prefer list_cluster_user_credentials for day-to-day work; this one is the break-glass credential and is disabled on clusters with local accounts turned off.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

server_fqdn.description: Return the kubeconfig against a private cluster's private FQDN instead of the public one.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The admin kubeconfig files, base64-encoded.

kubeconfigs.description: Each with name and value; value is the base64 kubeconfig.

list_cluster_user_credentials.title: Get a cluster's user kubeconfig
list_cluster_user_credentials.description: Return the user kubeconfig for the cluster, base64-encoded. On an Entra-integrated cluster this config prompts for a login and the caller's Kubernetes RBAC applies, which is what you want for normal access. Use format "exec" for the kubelogin plugin form, or "azure" for the legacy one.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

format.description: Credential format -- exec for the kubelogin plugin, azure for the legacy form.

server_fqdn.description: Return the kubeconfig against a private cluster's private FQDN instead of the public one.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The user kubeconfig files, base64-encoded.

kubeconfigs.description: Each with name and value; value is the base64 kubeconfig.

list_cluster_monitoring_user_credentials.title: Get a cluster's monitoring kubeconfig
list_cluster_monitoring_user_credentials.description: Return the kubeconfig bound to the cluster's monitoring user, which has read access to metrics and logs rather than to workloads. Use it for dashboards and scrapers that should not be able to change anything.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

server_fqdn.description: Return the kubeconfig against a private cluster's private FQDN instead of the public one.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The monitoring kubeconfig files, base64-encoded.

rotate_cluster_certificates.title: Rotate a cluster's certificates
rotate_cluster_certificates.description: Rotate the cluster's control plane and node certificates. Every existing kubeconfig stops working and must be fetched again, and the API server is briefly unavailable while it happens. Do this on a schedule or after a suspected compromise, not casually.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty; the rotation runs asynchronously, tracked by the azure-asyncoperation header.

rotate_service_account_signing_keys.title: Rotate a cluster's service account signing keys
rotate_service_account_signing_keys.description: Rotate the keys the cluster signs Kubernetes service account tokens with. Every issued token is invalidated, so workloads using workload identity must obtain new ones -- expect disruption until pods restart.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty; the rotation runs asynchronously, tracked by the azure-asyncoperation header.

get_upgrade_profile.title: Get a cluster's available upgrades
get_upgrade_profile.description: Report which Kubernetes versions the cluster's control plane and each node pool can move to next, and whether each is preview. Read this before setting kubernetes_version, since AKS only allows one minor version step at a time.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The upgrade options for the control plane and each node pool.

properties.description: controlPlaneProfile with kubernetesVersion and upgrades, plus agentPoolProfiles.

run_command.title: Run a kubectl command in the cluster
run_command.description: Execute a command inside the cluster from the management plane, without network access to the API server -- the standard way to reach a private cluster. command is a kubectl invocation such as "kubectl get pods -A"; context can carry a base64 zip of manifests for "kubectl apply -f .". Returns 202 with an id; read the output with get_command_result. This runs with cluster-admin rights, so it can change anything.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

cluster_name.description: Name of the cluster to run the command in.

command.description: The kubectl command to run, e.g. "kubectl get pods --all-namespaces".

context.description: Base64-encoded zip of files the command needs, mounted in its working directory.

cluster_token.description: Entra ID token to run the command as, instead of the cluster's admin identity.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The accepted command, whose id is passed to get_command_result.

properties.description: provisioningState, exitCode, startedAt, finishedAt and logs once finished.

get_command_result.title: Get the result of a cluster command
get_command_result.description: Fetch the outcome of a run_command invocation: its exit code, how long it took, and the command's combined output in logs. A 202 means it is still running -- poll until you get 200.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

cluster_name.description: Name of the cluster the command ran in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The command's exit code, timing and output.

properties.description: provisioningState, exitCode, startedAt, finishedAt, logs, reason.

abort_latest_operation.title: Abort the cluster's running operation
abort_latest_operation.description: Cancel the long-running operation currently in flight on a cluster -- an upgrade or scale that is stuck. The cluster is left in a Canceled provisioning state and must be reconciled with another create_or_update_managed_cluster before further changes.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

cluster_name.description: Name of the cluster whose operation to abort.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty; the abort itself is asynchronous, tracked by the azure-asyncoperation header.

list_agent_pools.title: List a cluster's node pools
list_agent_pools.description: List the node pools attached to a cluster, each with its VM size, node count, autoscaling bounds, Kubernetes and node image versions, mode (System or User) and provisioning state.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The cluster's node pools.

items.description: name and properties (count, vmSize, mode, osType, orchestratorVersion, nodeImageVersion, enableAutoScaling, minCount, maxCount).

get_agent_pool.title: Get a node pool
get_agent_pool.description: Read one node pool's configuration -- count, VM size, OS type and SKU, disk size and type, taints and labels, autoscaling bounds, upgrade settings and provisioning state.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The node pool resource.

create_or_update_agent_pool.title: Create, scale or upgrade a node pool
create_or_update_agent_pool.description: Add a node pool to a cluster, or change an existing one -- this single call covers scaling (count), autoscaling (enable_auto_scaling with min_count and max_count) and upgrading (orchestrator_version). A full PUT, so read the pool with get_agent_pool first and send it back amended. Asynchronous; scaling down cordons and drains nodes, which takes time.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

agent_pool_name.description: Name of the node pool to create or update.

count.description: Number of nodes in the pool. With autoscaling on, this is the current size.

vm_size.description: VM size for the nodes, e.g. Standard_DS2_v2. Immutable after creation.

mode.description: System pools host cluster services; User pools host workloads.

os_type.description: Node operating system. Immutable after creation.

os_sku.description: OS image family for the nodes, e.g. Ubuntu or AzureLinux.

os_disk_size_gb.description: OS disk size in GB. Immutable after creation.

os_disk_type.description: Ephemeral is faster and free but lost on reimage; Managed persists.

pool_type.description: Whether the pool is a virtual machine scale set or availability set.

orchestrator_version.description: Kubernetes version for this pool. Raising it upgrades the pool's nodes.

enable_auto_scaling.description: Let the cluster autoscaler size the pool between min_count and max_count.

min_count.description: Smallest node count the autoscaler may go to.

max_count.description: Largest node count the autoscaler may go to.

max_pods.description: Maximum pods per node. Immutable after creation.

availability_zones.description: Availability zones to spread nodes across, e.g. ["1","2","3"].

node_taints.description: Kubernetes taints applied to every node, e.g. ["sku=gpu:NoSchedule"].

node_labels.description: Kubernetes labels applied to every node in the pool.

vnet_subnet_id.description: ARM id of the subnet the nodes join. Immutable after creation.

scale_set_priority.description: Spot nodes are much cheaper but can be evicted at any time.

tags.description: Tags applied to the pool's underlying Azure resources.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The node pool as accepted, with provisioning in progress.

delete_agent_pool.title: Delete a node pool
delete_agent_pool.description: Remove a node pool from a cluster. Its nodes are cordoned, drained and deleted, so anything running there is rescheduled elsewhere -- or stays Pending if no other pool can take it. The cluster's last System pool cannot be deleted.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

agent_pool_name.description: Name of the node pool to delete.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty; deletion runs asynchronously, tracked by the azure-asyncoperation header.

get_agent_pool_upgrade_profile.title: Get a node pool's available upgrades
get_agent_pool_upgrade_profile.description: Report which Kubernetes versions a node pool can move to next, and the latest node image version available to it. Read this before setting orchestrator_version on the pool.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The versions this node pool can upgrade to.

upgrade_node_image_version.title: Upgrade a node pool's node image
upgrade_node_image_version.description: Reimage the pool's nodes onto the latest node image without changing the Kubernetes version -- this is how OS and runtime security patches get applied. Nodes are cordoned, drained and replaced in surge batches, so workloads move but the pool stays available.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

agent_pool_name.description: Name of the node pool to reimage.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The pool as accepted, with the upgrade running asynchronously.

abort_agent_pool_operation.title: Abort a node pool's running operation
abort_agent_pool_operation.description: Cancel the long-running operation in flight on one node pool -- a scale or upgrade that is stuck. The pool ends in a Canceled provisioning state and needs a further create_or_update_agent_pool to reconcile.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

agent_pool_name.description: Name of the node pool whose operation to abort.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty; the abort itself is asynchronous, tracked by the azure-asyncoperation header.

get_available_agent_pool_versions.title: List Kubernetes versions available to a cluster's node pools
get_available_agent_pool_versions.description: List the Kubernetes versions new or upgraded node pools on this cluster may use, with the default and any that are preview. Narrower than list_kubernetes_versions, which answers for the region rather than the cluster.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The Kubernetes versions this cluster's node pools may run.

properties.description: agentPoolVersions, each with kubernetesVersion, default and isPreview.

list_outbound_network_dependencies.title: List a cluster's required outbound endpoints
list_outbound_network_dependencies.description: List the endpoints a cluster's nodes must be able to reach for it to work -- registries, Entra ID, the AKS control plane. Exactly what a firewall or network security group needs to allow, so read this before locking egress down.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The outbound endpoints the cluster requires, grouped by category.

items.description: category and endpoints, each with domainName and endpointDetails (ipAddress, port, protocol).

list_maintenance_configurations.title: List a cluster's maintenance windows
list_maintenance_configurations.description: List the maintenance configurations on a cluster. These are the windows in which AKS may apply automatic upgrades and node image patches -- aksManagedAutoUpgradeSchedule for cluster upgrades, aksManagedNodeOSUpgradeSchedule for node OS patching.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The cluster's maintenance configurations.

items.description: name and properties (maintenanceWindow or timeInWeek, notAllowedTime).

get_maintenance_configuration.title: Get a maintenance window
get_maintenance_configuration.description: Read one maintenance configuration -- its schedule, duration, time zone and any blackout periods during which AKS must not touch the cluster.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The maintenance configuration.

create_or_update_maintenance_configurati.title: Set a maintenance window
create_or_update_maintenance_configurati.description: Define when AKS may apply automatic upgrades to a cluster. Use the name aksManagedAutoUpgradeSchedule for Kubernetes upgrades and aksManagedNodeOSUpgradeSchedule for node OS patching; maintenance_window carries the schedule, duration, start time and time zone, plus any not-allowed date ranges.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

config_name.description: Configuration name -- aksManagedAutoUpgradeSchedule for cluster upgrades, aksManagedNodeOSUpgradeSchedule for node OS patching.

maintenance_window.description: The window: schedule (daily, weekly, absoluteMonthly or relativeMonthly), durationHours, utcOffset, startDate and startTime, plus notAllowedDates.

time_in_week.description: Legacy weekly schedule form -- day plus hour slots. Prefer maintenance_window.

not_allowed_time.description: Legacy blackout ranges, each with start and end. Prefer maintenance_window.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The maintenance configuration as stored.

delete_maintenance_configuration.title: Delete a maintenance window
delete_maintenance_configuration.description: Remove a maintenance configuration. Automatic upgrades governed by it revert to running at any time, so delete one only when the schedule is genuinely no longer wanted.

resource_group.description: Resource group the cluster is in.

config_name.description: Name of the maintenance configuration to delete.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty -- 200 when deleted, 204 when it was already gone.

list_kubernetes_versions.title: List Kubernetes versions available in a region
list_kubernetes_versions.description: List the Kubernetes versions AKS offers in a region, with each one's support plan, patch releases and whether it is preview or being retired. Answers for the region as a whole -- use get_upgrade_profile for what a specific cluster may move to next.

location.description: Azure region to ask about, e.g. westeurope.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The Kubernetes versions available in the region.

values.description: Each with version, capabilities, isPreview and patchVersions.

get_os_options.title: List node OS options in a region
get_os_options.description: List the operating system SKUs AKS supports for node pools in a region, and whether each supports FIPS. Read this before setting os_sku on a node pool, since availability varies by region.

location.description: Azure region to ask about, e.g. westeurope.

resource_type.description: Resource type to report options for -- managedClusters.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The OS options available for node pools in the region.

properties.description: osOptionPropertyList, each with osType and enableFipsImage.

list_snapshots.title: List node pool snapshots
list_snapshots.description: List the node pool snapshots in the subscription. A snapshot captures a node pool's configuration and node image so a new pool can be created from exactly that state, which is how a known-good image version is pinned.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: Every node pool snapshot in the subscription.

items.description: id, name, location and properties (creationData, kubernetesVersion, nodeImageVersion, vmSize, osType).

get_snapshot.title: Get a node pool snapshot
get_snapshot.description: Read one snapshot's captured configuration -- the source node pool, the Kubernetes and node image versions, VM size, OS type and SKU it recorded.

resource_group.description: Resource group the snapshot is in.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The snapshot resource.

create_snapshot.title: Create a node pool snapshot
create_snapshot.description: Capture an existing node pool's configuration and node image version, so later pools can be created from exactly that state. source_resource_id is the full ARM id of the node pool being captured.

resource_group.description: Resource group to create the snapshot in.

location.description: Azure region for the snapshot, e.g. westeurope.

source_resource_id.description: Full ARM id of the node pool to capture.

snapshot_type.description: What is being captured. NodePool is the supported value.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The snapshot as created.

delete_snapshot.title: Delete a node pool snapshot
delete_snapshot.description: Remove a snapshot. Node pools already created from it are unaffected, but no new pool can be created from that captured state afterwards.

resource_group.description: Resource group the snapshot is in.

snapshot_name.description: Name of the snapshot to delete.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: Empty -- 200 when deleted, 204 when it was already gone.

list_operations.title: List Microsoft.ContainerService operations
list_operations.description: List every ARM operation the AKS provider exposes, with the display name of each. Useful for identifying which role action a 403 is actually complaining about.

api_version.description: Microsoft.ContainerService ARM API version to call.

output.description: The provider's available operations.

items.description: name and display (provider, resource, operation, description).
